requirement:
A provider failure that ends the model conversation returns
`ValidationError::Agent` to the awaiting ask builder.
rationale:
The requirement has one obligation. When a provider failure ends the model conversation, the awaiting ask builder gets `ValidationError::Agent`.

- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[assistant_text_and_provider_failure_cannot_become_typed_results]` covers the direct case. It uses a `ToolAgent` over `Script::new(vec![None])`. The `Script` provider's `complete` returns `io::Error::other("permanent provider failure")` once its script is exhausted. The test then asserts that `ctx.ask::<bool>().await` returns `Err(ValidationError::Agent(error))` and that the error text contains "permanent provider failure". It also asserts that no dependencies were recorded. That checks both the variant and that the provider's error reaches the caller.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[configured_agents_initialize_only_when_asked_and_report_setup_errors]` covers a second path through the configured agent. A missing credential makes the awaited `validation::verify` return `ValidationError::Agent` whose message names the credential variable. This is a setup failure rather than a mid-conversation one, but it still checks that the awaiting caller receives the `Agent` variant.

The requirement distinguishes no other failure kinds or modes. The same test also exercises the text-only no-submission case, but that case belongs to other requirements. Both tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, so there is no marking gap.
